source_review.notes: Reviewed Carnegie Mellon's Jacobson thesis record, the Raman-Raman-Rao indexable-dictionary paper, Navarro's author-maintained book and rank/select paper, the current engineering paper, the SDSL design paper, and maintained SDSL-lite repository. All seven final destinations returned HTTP 200. Bounds and implementation claims remain scoped to their stated computational model or named implementation.

evidence: Checked B[0..n), access, half-open rank, zero-based select, m, block/superblock, class/offset, and redundancy notation.
Checked validity domains distinguish positions 0..n for rank from positions 0..n-1 for access/select results.
Checked succinct n+o(n), density-sensitive log binomial, and practical byte accounting are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter declares conventions before using inverse identities and explicitly warns that cited libraries may use different conventions.

evidence: Recomputed fixture totals, superblock counts [0,4,8,12,16], and block-relative counts [0,3,0,1,0,2,0,1,0].
Recomputed rank1(17)=9, rank0(17)=8, select1 ordinals 0/7/15 as 0/14/31, and select0 ordinals 0/7 as 1/15.
Recomputed exercise bit positions, ranks 0/2/5, and every inverse for B=011010011.
Recomputed billion-bit directory estimates as 1.953125 MB plus 25.390625 MB, and 152.34375 MB including payload.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Capacity arithmetic uses decimal MB and intentionally ignores ceilings only where the exercise requests an estimate.

evidence: Derived rank0(i)=i-rank1(i) for a binary half-open prefix.
Derived both rank/select inverse identities from the count before and through a selected position.
Verified superblock redundancy O(n/log n) and block redundancy O(n log log n/log n) are o(n).
Verified half-log residual patterns number sqrt(n), so a polylogarithmic table per pattern is o(n).
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Constant time is qualified by a word RAM with sufficiently wide words and declared constant-time operations or included universal tables.

evidence: Reviewed empty, all-zero, all-one, singleton, alternating, sparse, dense, clustered, and duplicate-boundary bit patterns.
Reviewed rank endpoints, invalid select ordinals, word/block/superblock boundaries, 65-bit padding, undefined full-word shifts, and counter overflow.
Reviewed byte/bit order, native-struct padding, instruction availability, mapped offset arithmetic, truncation, checksums, and corrupt directories.
Reviewed static bit flips, dynamic summary propagation, snapshot isolation, construction peak, cross-platform mapping, and cache/NUMA behavior.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model uses a byte string, tiny directories, residual scans, and binary-search select; it excludes packed words, ISA paths, compression, mutation, mapping, and corruption.

evidence: The model derives all prefix counts from the 32 logical bits and constructs directory entries exactly at eight/four-bit boundaries.
Rank partitions each prefix into nonoverlapping superblock, relative block, and residual components.
Binary-search select is checked for both bit values and all sixteen valid ordinals each.
All access-at-select and before/through rank inverse properties plus exact twenty-one-line output pass.
invariant_checking.notes: The model validates semantics and accounting rather than asymptotic succinctness or constant-time select.

evidence: Reviewed two-level rank decomposition and redundancy term derivations.
Reviewed select sampling rationale and why irregular spacing prevents a position-only rank directory from directly solving select.
Reviewed information baseline n for arbitrary bit vectors and log2 binomial(n,m) for fixed-density sets.
Reviewed dynamic summary and immutable-generation arguments needed to preserve prefix semantics after mutation/publication.
proof_review.notes: No concrete constant-time select construction, lower-bound proof, compressed-format optimality, lock-free algorithm, or persistent implementation proof is claimed.

evidence: Asymptotic word-RAM results are separated from finite implementation and memory-footprint claims.
RRR, Elias-Fano, run-length, and dynamic structures are labeled families/trade-offs rather than fully derived implementations.
Residual scanning and binary-search select in the fixture explicitly disclaim constant-time succinct behavior.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Practical recommendations are benchmark and validation obligations, not consequences of asymptotic bounds.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact twenty-one-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the safe verifier.
Independent calculations reproduced directory entries, all queried ranks/selects/inverses, exercise vectors, and capacity estimates.
All seven reference destinations returned HTTP 200 and local structure, links, examples, exercises, answers, and snippet checks passed before review.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No packed C/C++ implementation, SDSL run, ISA benchmark, exhaustive all-pattern campaign, compressed representation, dynamic concurrency test, mapped-file corruption campaign, or production deployment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter anchors rank/select in one explicit convention, derives static rank redundancy, separates select engineering, and follows through compression, mutation, persistence, applications, and validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed bit/byte/word layout, padding and overflow, ISA dispatch, layout/cache, representation choice, streaming construction, portable serialization, mapped validation, immutable publication, dynamic alternatives, corruption, and capacity evidence.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet fixes conventions and invariants; the executable fixture exposes directories and inverse properties; ten examples cover off-by-one, padding, density, overflow, mutation, corruption, and composition; five exercises span computation, proof, capacity, selection, and file-format design.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/author/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Jacobson, Raman, Satti, Navarro, Providel, Kurpicz, Gog, SDSL, database, information-retrieval, systems, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither a production constant-time succinct rank/select implementation, compressed optimality, portable ISA behavior, dynamic concurrency, mapped-file security, certification, nor deployment fitness.
